entities.evidence: Noah survives the flood with those in the ark. This identifies the son of Lamech named in Genesis 5:29 and agrees with the source tag.

review.translation: [So he wiped out|0] [every|2,1] [living thing|3] [that|4] {was} [on|5] [the surface of|6] [the ground|7], [from humans|8] [to|9] [four-footed beasts|10], [to|11] [crawling creatures|12], [and even to|13] [the birds of|14] [the sky|15]. [They were wiped|16] [from|17] [the earth|18], [and|19] [only|20] [Noah|21] [and|22] {those} [who|22] {were} [with him|23] [in the ark|24] [survived|19].

analysis.evidence: The direct object אֶת כָּל הַיְקוּם includes humans, livestock, creeping things, and birds. The passive וַיִּמָּחוּ מִן הָאָרֶץ confirms the result: they were wiped from the earth. Only Noah and those with him in the ark remained.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־ and apocopation of the final ה.
analysis.sense: Wipe out living beings from the face of the earth.

analysis.evidence: אֶת introduces כָּל הַיְקוּם, “everything that existed,” as the definite direct object of וַיִּמַח, “he wiped out.”
analysis.morphology: Unsuffixed direct-object particle in the short form אֶת.

analysis.evidence: In אֶת כָּל הַיְקוּם, כָּל modifies the singular collective הַיְקוּם. The list of humans, livestock, creeping things, and birds spells out what “all” includes.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular construct noun, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: כָּל הַיְקוּם means “every living thing.” The verse identifies what was wiped out by listing humans, livestock, creeping things, and birds.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הַ־ prefixed to a masculine singular absolute noun used collectively.

analysis.evidence: אֲשֶׁר introduces a relative clause modifying כָּל הַיְקוּם, “every living thing.” The clause עַל פְּנֵי הָאֲדָמָה supplies its location, giving the reading “every living thing that was on the face of the ground.”
analysis.morphology: Uninflected relative particle

analysis.evidence: In אֲשֶׁר עַל פְּנֵי הָאֲדָמָה, “that was on the face of the ground,” עַל introduces פְּנֵי הָאֲדָמָה and locates what was wiped out.
analysis.morphology: Simple preposition without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In עַל פְּנֵי הָאֲדָמָה, “on the surface of the ground,” פְּנֵי is the construct form bound to הָאֲדָמָה. The phrase locates the living things that were wiped out.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, both genders, plural construct, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In עַל פְּנֵי הָאֲדָמָה, “on the face of the ground,” פְּנֵי is in construct with הָאֲדָמָה. The phrase identifies the surface on which the living beings were wiped out.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, feminine singular absolute, with prefixed definite article הָ־.
analysis.sense: the ground underfoot; the face of the earth

analysis.evidence: מֵאָדָם begins a range that continues with עַד בְּהֵמָה, עַד רֶמֶשׂ, and וְעַד עוֹף הַשָּׁמַיִם. The verse lists the kinds of living beings swept away, with humans as the first group.
analysis.morphology: Prefixed preposition מִן in the form מֵ־, followed by a masculine singular absolute noun used collectively.

analysis.evidence: In מֵאָדָם עַד בְּהֵמָה, “from humans to livestock,” עַד introduces livestock as the next group included among those wiped out. The list continues with creeping things and birds.
analysis.morphology: Uninflected preposition with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: even to, extending the range to include a named category

analysis.evidence: The verse lists בְּהֵמָה between אָדָם (humankind) and רֶמֶשׂ (creeping things), followed by עוֹף הַשָּׁמַיִם (birds of the sky). In this account of all life wiped from the ground, the singular names four-footed beasts collectively, with no restriction to livestock.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, feminine singular absolute, used collectively, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: After מֵאָדָם עַד בְּהֵמָה (“from humans to livestock”), the marked עַד introduces רֶמֶשׂ (“creeping things”), extending the list of living things wiped out. The list continues with וְעַד עוֹף הַשָּׁמַיִם (“and to the birds of the sky”).
analysis.morphology: Simple preposition without prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: even to, extending the range to include a named category

analysis.evidence: The repeated עַד introduces successive groups. רֶמֶשׂ stands between בְּהֵמָה (livestock) and עוֹף הַשָּׁמַיִם (birds of the sky), so the singular noun denotes creeping creatures collectively.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine singular absolute, used collectively.

analysis.evidence: The list begins with מֵאָדָם, “from humankind,” and ends with וְעַד עוֹף הַשָּׁמַיִם, “and even to the birds of the sky.” The final עַד marks birds as the last category included among the living things wiped out.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וְ prefixed to the preposition עַד.
analysis.sense: even to, as many as, to the point of

analysis.evidence: עוֹף הַשָּׁמַיִם means “the birds of the sky.” The phrase follows בְּהֵמָה and רֶמֶשׂ in a list of living creatures, so the singular עוֹף designates birds as a class.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine singular construct, used collectively.

analysis.evidence: In עוֹף הַשָּׁמַיִם, “birds of the sky,” the marked noun identifies where the birds fly. The phrase completes the verse’s list of creatures swept away by the flood.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הַ־ prefixed to a masculine plural noun in the absolute state.

analysis.evidence: The opening וַיִּמַח takes אֶת־כָּל־הַיְקוּם as its object. The plural passive וַיִּמָּחוּ refers back to the humans and animals just listed and says what happened to them. מִן־הָאָרֶץ specifies that they were wiped out from the earth.
analysis.morphology: Niphal wayyiqtol, third-person masculine plural, with prefixed וַ and plural ending וּ.
analysis.sense: Wipe out living beings from the face of the earth.

analysis.evidence: In וַיִּמָּחוּ מִן הָאָרֶץ, “they were wiped from the earth,” מִן introduces הָאָרֶץ as the place from which the living beings were removed.
analysis.morphology: Independent preposition without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: מִן הָאָרֶץ means “from the earth.” It names the place from which the people and creatures previously described as living עַל פְּנֵי הָאֲדָמָה (“on the face of the ground”) were wiped out. Only Noah and those with him in the ark remained.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, singular absolute, common gender, with prefixed definite article הָ־.

analysis.evidence: After וַיִּמָּחוּ describes the living things being wiped from the earth, אַךְ singles out Noah and those with him in the ark as the only ones who remained alive.
analysis.morphology: Niphal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ and no suffix.

analysis.evidence: After the verse says that all living things on the ground were wiped out, אַךְ limits the subject of וַיִשָּׁאֶר to נֹחַ וַאֲשֶׁר אִתּוֹ בַּתֵּבָה. Only Noah and those with him in the ark remained.
analysis.morphology: Restrictive particle with no prefix or suffix.

draft.change: Add a personal-name article for נֹחַ linked to the root article nuach.
draft.definition: Noah, the son whom Lamech names in hope of relief from toil.
draft.evidence: Genesis 5:29 gives the name נֹחַ and explains it through the wordplay on יְנַחֲמֵנוּ, “he will comfort us.”

analysis.evidence: In וַיִּשָּׁאֶר אַךְ נֹחַ, Noah is the named subject of וַיִּשָּׁאֶר, “remained.” The phrase וַאֲשֶׁר אִתּוֹ בַּתֵּבָה adds those who were with him in the ark.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular proper noun without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: וַאֲשֶׁר אִתּוֹ בַּתֵּבָה means ‘and those who were with him in the ark.’ The phrase is coordinated with נֹחַ as a subject of וַיִּשָּׁאֶר ‘remained.’ The relative clause supplies its own referent.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וַ־ ‘and’ prefixed to the indeclinable relative particle אֲשֶׁר, used substantivally.

draft.change: Add Genesis 7:23 to the existing company sense of the preposition אֵת.
draft.evidence: Genesis 7:23 identifies the survivors alongside Noah as those who were אִתּוֹ, with him, in the ark.

analysis.evidence: In נֹחַ וַאֲשֶׁר אִתּוֹ בַּתֵּבָה, Noah and those who were with him in the ark are the ones who remained. אִתּוֹ identifies whose company they were in, and בַּתֵּבָה gives their location.
analysis.morphology: Preposition in its suffixed form אִתּ־ with the third-person masculine singular pronominal suffix וֹ, referring to Noah.

draft.change: Add תֵּבָה under its own consonants, תבה. The flood narrative supplies the sense directly, and the source tag תאר has no demonstrated connection to this noun.
draft.definition: The ark in which Noah, his household, and the animals survived the flood.
draft.evidence: Genesis 7:18 describes the ark floating on the water. Genesis 7:23 identifies its occupants as the survivors.

analysis.evidence: וַיִּשָּׁאֶר אַךְ נֹחַ וַאֲשֶׁר אִתּוֹ identifies the survivors as Noah and those with him. בַּתֵּבָה locates them inside the ark already described as floating on the waters in Genesis 7:18.
analysis.morphology: Locative preposition בְּ with the definite article הַ, fused as בַּ and doubling the following ת, plus a feminine singular absolute common noun.
analysis.sense: The vessel that carried Noah and those with him through the flood.
